# Didache Chapter 16 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Hierosolymitanus (H), Didache 16 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/DID_016_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 16

**1** Watch over your life — let your lamps not be quenched and let your loins not be ungirded, but be ready — for you do not know the hour at which our Lord comes.

**2** And gather together frequently, seeking the things that are appropriate for your souls; for the whole time of your faith will be of no profit to you unless you are made perfect at the last time.

**3** For in the last days the false prophets and corrupters will be multiplied, and the sheep will be turned into wolves, and love will be turned into hatred.

**4** For as lawlessness increases, they will hate and persecute and betray one another, and then the world-deceiver will appear as a son of God, and he will perform signs and wonders, and the earth will be given over into his hands, and he will commit lawless deeds such as have never occurred since the beginning of the age.

**5** Then humankind will come into the fire of testing, and many will stumble and perish; but those who endure in their faith will be saved by the Curse itself.

**6** And then the signs of the truth will appear: first the sign of opening in heaven; then the sign of the sound of a trumpet; and third, the resurrection of the dead —

**7** but not of all the dead, but as it has been said: "The Lord will come, and all the holy ones with him."

**8** Then the world will see the Lord coming upon the clouds of heaven.

---

*EMET notes: V.1 — "let your loins not be ungirded" = be dressed and ready for action (a Jewish idiom; cf. Ex 12:11; Luke 12:35). V.4 — "world-deceiver" (κοσμοπλάνης) = a compound unique to the Didache (also in Epistle of Barnabas 4:1) for the Antichrist figure. "Son of God" — the deceiver claims divine sonship. V.5 — "the Curse itself" (ὑπ᾽ αὐτῆς τῆς κατάρας) is remarkably difficult. Some manuscripts and scholars read this as "saved by the One who was cursed" (i.e., Christ, who became a curse for us, Gal 3:13). This remains one of the most debated phrases in the Didache. V.6-7 — three eschatological signs: opening of heaven, trumpet, resurrection. V.7 quotes Zech 14:5 LXX ("the Lord my God will come, and all the holy ones with him"). V.8 — echoes Dan 7:13 and Matt 24:30 ("coming on the clouds of heaven").*
